transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon.
We have a status report this morning of the economic effects of AI after last week's dive
on the stock market, and PR Scott Horsley has details.
Futures markets suggest we could see a rebound this morning.
Investors might go bargain hunting after last week's steep drop when all the major stock
indexes dropped by 8% or more.
Investors were dumping stocks last week, even as Anthropik, the company behind the popular
AI chatbot Claude, was raising a boatload of money by selling shares to the public for
the first time.
It just highlights, once again, the real uncertainty investors are feeling about the huge sums
of money that are being plowed into artificial intelligence at a time when no one's really
sure if that big bet's going to pay off.
The National Association for Business Economics is out with a new survey on AI.
It finds one in five businesses reported widespread productivity gains as a result of AI.
About half said gains from using AI in their businesses were not widespread.
Ukraine says it carried out an attack on a Russian warship docked at a port in Libya.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the attack an exemplary Ukrainian operation
in response to Russia's war.
Russia has not yet commented.
And Peyar's Ayobotrawi has more.
Zelensky says the warship was targeted by seven Ukrainian-made naval drones.
He says the ship sank and that a combat helicopter was also destroyed.
Libya says the Russian ship had been docked for refueling and resupplying at a naval port
in the eastern city of Benghazi when it was attacked and caught fire.
Libya's eastern government condemned the attack at its port, calling it an assault on Libya's
sovereignty and stressing that the North African country is not a party to the Russia-Ukraine
war.
Russia backs the eastern Libya government and has a foothold there.
The Ukrainian attack on the port threatens to expand the war, now in its fifth year.
Libya is more than 1,500 miles south of Ukraine and it's unclear where in the Mediterranean
sea the naval drones were launched from.
Ayobotrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
This Thanksgiving week, the National Weather Service is predicting severe weather in many
parts of the country.
Here's Andrea Shue.
On the west coast, a confluence of two things could bring flooding, rain fueled by wide
bands of moisture, and king tides expected to be among the highest tides this year.
Western Oklahoma, Texas, the Great Lakes, and New England could see snow, the southeast
and the east coast heavy wind and rain.
Matthew Capucci, senior meteorologist with MyRadar, says altogether it's shaping up
to be quite the week.
It's going to start eventful on one coast and kind of end eventful on the other coast,
unfortunately.
The delays are likely.
AAA expects some 81 million Americans to travel this Thanksgiving.
Nearly six million are expected to fly.
Andrea Shue, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR News.
A local wardrobe workers union in New York has voted to authorize a strike just as Broadway
moves into the lucrative holiday season.
The move comes weeks after union stage hands voted to do the same.
Jeff London reports.
Both locals, which are members of the International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees, or
IATSI, have been working without contracts since July.
The locals have been negotiating with the Broadway League, which represents theater
owners and producers, but no agreements have been reached.
A strike authorization is not the same as a strike, but with Broadway still in recovery
mode following an 18-month closure during the pandemic, a work stoppage around the period
from Thanksgiving to New Year's could cause great economic damage and a disruption for
audiences, many of whom travel to New York to see Broadway shows.
For NPR News, I'm Jeff London in New York.
If you just happen to have a few million dollars lying around, you could be the proud new owner
of Batman's Ride.
That mobile used in Tim Burton's 1992 movie Batman Returns goes up for auction today.
Julian's auctions estimates that it could bring in five to seven million dollars.
The glossy black car appeared in most of the film's driving scenes and still has its original
paint, a Chevy V8 engine, and a flame shooting exhaust system, but there is a catch.
The car is not street legal.
I'm Lyndy Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.
[BLANK_AUDIO]

topics.text: AI-driven stock market dive last week, with futures suggesting a possible rebound
National Association for Business Economics survey finds one in five businesses report widespread AI productivity gains
Ukraine says it attacked a Russian warship docked at a Libyan port in Benghazi
National Weather Service predicts severe Thanksgiving week weather, including west coast flooding and king tides
Broadway wardrobe workers in New York vote to authorize a strike ahead of holiday season
Batman Returns Batmobile goes up for auction, estimated to bring five to seven million dollars
